blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights Gandalf, an intelligent analytics service deployed at Microsoft Azure for safe software rollouts. Gandalf processes over 20TB of data daily to monitor deployments, detecting issues by analyzing platform events, API calls, and fault types. It operates on a lambda architecture with fast and slow paths to identify immediate and latent problems, respectively. Gandalf's transparency and interactive evidence access have built trust among development teams, reducing deployment times by half. The paper emphasizes the challenges of spotting bad rollouts in large-scale, ever-changing systems, including ambient faults, delayed issues, and complex causal relationships. Gandalf's three-phase pipeline—anomaly detection, correlation analysis, and decision engine—addresses these challenges, using techniques like Holt-Winters forecasting and ensemble voting with vetoes to pinpoint faulty components.
paper_title: Gandalf: An Intelligent, End-to-End Analytics Service for Safe Deployment in Cloud-Scale Infrastructure
paper_abstract: Modern cloud systems have a vast number of components that continuously undergo updates. Deploying these frequent updates quickly without breaking the system is challenging. In this paper, we present Gandalf, an end-to-end analytics service for safe deployment in a large-scale system infrastructure. Gandalf enables rapid and robust impact assessment of software rollouts to catch bad rollouts before they cause widespread outages. Gandalf monitors and analyzes various fault signals. It will correlate each signal against all the ongoing rollouts using a spatial and temporal correlation algorithm. The core decision logic of Gandalf includes an ensemble ranking algorithm that determines which rollout may have caused the fault signals, and a binary classifier that assesses the impact of the fault signals. The analysis result will decide whether a rollout is safe to proceed or should be stopped. By using a lambda architecture, Gandalf provides both realtime and long-term deployment monitoring with automated decisions and notifications. Gandalf has been running in production in Microsoft Azure for more than 18 months, serving both data-plane and control-plane components. It achieves 92.4% precision and 100% recall (no high-impact service outages in Azure Compute were caused by bad rollouts) for dataplane rollouts. For control-plane rollouts, Gandalf achieves 94.9% precision and 99.8% recall.
